evidence.text: Service: MEDICINE
Allergies: Simvastatin
Weakness, leg pain

___ M w/ hx post-laminectomy pain syndrome, BPH, COPD, 
depression, etoh abuse, gout, HL, PVD, restless leg syndrome p/w 
b/l leg pain.

Pt has had b/l ___ burning pain from his knees to 
his feet for several months but worsened today.

Pt normally 
ambulates w/ walker but has had increasingly frequent falls due 
to b/l leg pain.
No dizziness or prodromal symptoms.
Pt fell at
4am due to leg pain, no headstrike, and fell yesterday as well.
Intermittent pitting edema for the past several months.

He has 
had urinary retention since his laminectomy ___ yrs ago and is 
followed by urology.

Takes morphine and oxycodone daily for 
pain, which has not been working.

Pt then came to the ED for 
evaluation.
Initial vitals in the ED: 99.0 104 155/66 20 97%.

Pt reportedly had pursed lip breathing, with bilateral 
expiratory wheezing, also bilateral 1+ pitting edema to knees, 
dp pulses faint but palpable and neurologically intact.

Pt's 
labs including chem panel and CBC were normal.

Chest XR did not 
show significant pulmonary edema.

Pt was given lorazepam for 
anxiety, morphine 2mg iv x 1 which did not relieve pain, 
hydromorphone 1mg iv x 1, which did relieve pain, and 
nebulizers, prednisone 60mg po, and azithromycin 500mg po for
COPD exacerbation.

Pt was admitted to medicine for further 
management.

Upon arrival to the floor, Pt reports that he had severe leg 
pain and could not walk.

Pt says that his weight is usually 187 
lbs, but his currently weight is 195 lbs.

Pt denies any dyspnea, 
but looks dyspneic and his breathing through pursed lips.

States 
that his main concern is leg pain and leg weakness.

He usually 
ambulates with walker but has not been able to do so for the 
last 4 days.
Reports normal sensation.

No incontinence or 
retention.
No recent falls or trauma.

Denies any palpitations, 
chest pain.
No presyncopal symtoms or lightheadedness.

No 
fevers, no chills, no nausea or vomiting, no diarrhea, no 
dysuria.
Review of Systems: as above.
- Left L3, L4 laminectomy, L4-5 foraminotomy, L3 discectomy
- Chronic pain and gait instability
- COPD
- Alcohol abuse
- Depression
- Gout
- Hyperlipidemia
- Restless legs syndrome
- BPH

ADMISSION PHYSICAL EXAM:
GENERAL: overweight man in bed in mild respiratory distress
HEENT: PERRL, EOMI, CN2-12 intact, moist mucous membranes

CARDIAC: tachycardic rate, regular rhythm, normal S1/S2, no 
murmurs, gallops, or rubs
LUNG: diffuse expiratory wheezes bilaterally, poor air movement

ABDOMEN: mildly firm, non-tender, mildly distended, normal bowel 
sounds

BACK: non-tender to palpation of spinous processes or 
paraspinous muscles.
EXTREMITIES: 2+ edema bilaterally up to hips

NEURO: A&O x 3, CN II-XII intact, grossly normal sensation 
throughout, ___ strength in upper extremities, though weaker on
R, ___ strength in left leg, ___ strength in R leg.

Pt unable to 
stand to gauge Romberg.

Normal finger-nose-finger and heel shin 
tests bilaterally.

Pt repeatedly tapped R arm when tapping R 
foot on command.

SKIN: warm and well perfused, no excoriations or lesions, no 
rashes
DISCHARGE PHYSICAL EXAM:
GENERAL: overweight man resting comfortably
HEENT: PERRL, EOMI, moist mucous membranes

CARDIAC: regular rhythm, normal S1/S2, no murmurs, gallops, or 
rubs

LUNG: scant expiratory wheezes bilaterally, very poor air 
movement
ABDOMEN: firm, non-tender, mildly distended, normal bowel sounds

BACK: non-tender to palpation of spinous processes or 
paraspinous muscles.
EXTREMITIES: 1+ edema bilaterally up to hips

NEURO: A&O x 3, ___ strength in upper extremities, ___ strength 
in left leg, ___ strength in R leg.

SKIN: warm and well perfused, no excoriations or lesions, no 
rashes

IMAGING:
MRI brain ___:
IMPRESSION:

Bilateral small infarcts of different ages, ranging from late 
acute/subacute to chronic.

Nonspecific white matter 
abnormalities likely reflecting sequela of chronic small vessel 
ischemic disease.
CXR ___:

IMPRESSION:  New fullness of the right hilus, likely due to 
adenopathy.
CT of the chest with contrast is recommended.
Chest CT ___:
IMPRESSION:

Right pulmonary artery projects a little more laterally than 
usual and accounts for the prominent right hilum.

No significant 
adenopathy.
No change from ___.
MRA brain ___:
IMPRESSION:

1. Limited examination due to patient motion, the left vertebral 
artery is not clearly identified, probably due to occlusion or 
anatomical variation.

No aneurysms larger than 3 mm in size are 
seen, the major vascular, moderate narrowing of the basilar 
artery and posterior cerebral arteries is likely related to 
atherosclerotic disease.

2. Unchanged foci of slow diffusion in the precentral gyri 
bilaterally.
MRI T-spine ___:
IMPRESSION:

1.  The sagittal scout view demonstrates severe degenerative 
changes 
throughout the cervical spine as described above, partially 
evaluated in this examination, correlation with dedicated MRI of 
the cervical spine is 
recommended to evaluate the spinal cord are rule out spinal cord 
compression.

2.  The signal intensity throughout the thoracic spinal cord is 
normal with no evidence of focal or diffuse lesions, there is no 
evidence of spinal canal stenosis or neural foraminal narrowing 
throughout the thoracic spine.
MRI C and L spine ___:
IMPRESSION:

1.  Atlantoaxial joint pannus abuts the ventral aspect of the 
cervicomedullary junction without deformation or compression.

Indeterminate tubular structure in the posterior epidural space 
at the level of the posterior arch of C1 abuts the dorsal spinal 
cord without deformation or compression.

However, there is 
abnormal high T2 signal at the cervicomedullary junction, 
suggesting subtle edema or myelomalacia.

The cervicomedullary 
junction parenchyma as well as the indeterminate posterior 
epidural structure at C1, which may represent a synovial cyst, 
should be better assessed by contrast-enhanced MRI.

2.  Multilevel spondylolisthesis and degenerative disease in the 
cervical spine.

At C2-3, there is severe spinal stenosis with 
compression of the spinal cord.

Abnormal signal in the cord at 
this level is compatible with edema or myelomalacia.

Multilevel 
neural foraminal narrowing is also present.

3.  Scoliosis, multilevel mild retrolisthesis, and multilevel 
degenerative disease in the lumbar spine.

Epidural lipomatosis 
at L5-S1.

Severe compression of the thecal sac at L5-S1 and 
moderate compression of the thecal sac at L4-5.

Impingement of 
multiple nerve roots in the subarticular zones and neural 
foramina, as detailed above.
CTA neck ___:
IMPRESSION:

1. Overall moderate atherosclerotic disease with high-grade 
narrowing at the origin of the right vertebral artery, with 
degree of stenosis, difficult to estimate on this exam.

There is 
likely approximately 50% narrowing of the left subclavian artery 
at the thoracic outlet.

No other evidence of high-grade stenosis 
throughout the neck vasculature, with no internal carotid artery 
stenosis by NASCET criteria.

2. Severe degenerative disease of the cervical spine, as 
described above, 
better-characterized on the recent MRI of the cervical spine, 
dated ___.
3. Panlobular emphysema at the lung apices.
EGD ___:
Findings: Esophagus:

Mucosa: Erythema with linear ulcerations consistent with 
esophagitis.
Stomach:

Contents: Retained food in stomach obscuring complete 
visualization of gastric fundus.

Mucosa: Diffuse erythema, congestion and atrophy of the mucosa 
with no bleeding were noted in the stomach body and antrum.
These findings are compatible with gastritis.
Duodenum: Normal duodenum.
Impression: Esophagitis
Food in the stomach

Erythema, congestion and atrophy in the stomach body and antrum 
compatible with gastritis
Otherwise normal EGD to third part of the duodenum

___ M w/ hx post-laminectomy pain syndrome, BPH, COPD, 
depression, h/o EtOH abuse, gout, HL, PVD, restless leg syndrome 
who now presents with subacute lower extremity weakness and 
worsening of his leg pain as well as a COPD flare.
ACTIVE MEDICAL ISSUES:

# Cervical stenosis: Pt has a history of post-laminectomy pain 
syndrome (manifesting as chronic leg pain) and has extensive 
degenerative spinal disease.

MRI C-spine showed severe spinal 
stenosis and compression of spinal cord at C2-3.

Ortho spine was 
consulted and did not think operative management was warranted 
as this is likely chronic weakness.

The option of invasive 
surgery was discussed with patient and his wife, who did not 
want further surgical interventions.

# Cerebral vascular disease: Pt reported subacute worsening of 
his weakness causing him to stop driving.

MRI brain was obtained 
to evaluate for CVA and revealed multiple subacute infarcts.

Neuro was consulted and recommended additional imaging studies 
and evaluation of stroke risk factors.

MRA brain/CTA neck was 
notable for moderate atherosclerotic disease in the neck with 
high-grade narrowing high-grade narrowing at the origin of the 
right vertebral artery, with degree of stenosis, difficult to 
estimate.

HbA1c was 6.1% and lipid panel revealed good control 
on his LDL.
He was started on ASA 81 mg po daily.

TTE with 
bubble study revealed preserved EF but was non diagnostic for
PFO.

# Esphogitis: Pt with coffee-ground emesis overnight on evening 
of ___.
No lower GIB, rectal exam guaiac negative.

No prior 
hx of GI bleeding and denied current alcohol or NSAID use.

Pt 
had been on prednisone for COPD flare which may have 
contributed.

He was placed on IV PPI gtt, prednisone and aspirin 
were discontinued and GI was consulted.
An EGD was performed on
___ which showed esophagitis and patient was started on PPI
BID and sucralfate.
His aspirin was restarted.

He had no further 
episodes of hemetemesis and hct remained stable.

# Right hilus fullness: Patient found to have R hilus fullness 
on CXR on admission with recommendation for chest CT to further 
evaluate for lymphadenopathy.

Chest CT ___ showed no 
adenopathy or explanation for R hilar fullness.

He states that he is taking his currently 
prescribed meds, but he appeared to be having an acute 
exacerbation of his COPD on admission.

He states that his 
dyspnea always gets worse with his leg pain.
He was treated for

COPD exacerbation with azithromycin and prednisone plus standing 
nebs.

Prednisone was held on ___ (after 4 days of treatment) 
due to GI bleed as above and not restarted.

Pt intermittently 
required low O2 NC but was saturating well on room air by 
discharge.
He should continue duo nebs as needed.
CHRONIC ISSUES:

# Post-laminectomy pain syndrome: Pt reports having chronic 
severe bilateral leg pain ever since his operation several years 
ago.

He was continued on home morphine SR, oxycodone, 
tizanidine, and topiramate.

Lidocaine patch was also added to 
his shin.
Pt was seen by chronic pain service ___
# Depression: Continued home citalopram
# BPH: Continued home finasteride, oxybutynin, tamsulosin
# Hyperlipidemia: Continued home lovastatin.
LDL 58.
# Code: full, confirmed
# Emergency Contact: wife
